meta.title: Per-congressional-district impact of a $3,000 per-child CTC, 2026
meta.label: pe611
meta.configuration_note: Latest policyengine.py release: policyengine 6.1.1 bundle (policyengine-us 2.2.1; populace_us_2024 @ populace-us-2024-spm-20260915). Not yet deployed to the live app as of 2026-09-24. Second run of this configuration (adds share_gaining_over_1usd and household-level output); first run kept as out/districts_pe611_run1.json.

dataset_year_file.name: populace_us_2024-year-2026
dataset_year_file.note: Year-2026 file written by policyengine ensure_datasets from the certified source .h5 (input variables calculated for 2026).

household_level_output.note: Per-household 2026 baseline and reform household_net_income with weights and district, from this run.

reform.note: Single parameter changed; everything else is current law in the installed policyengine-us.

method.grouping_variable: congressional_district_geoid (household; SSDD integer, at-large states and DC use district 00)
method.weights: household_weight from the certified national dataset after ensure_datasets for 2026

fields.geoid: 4-character zero-padded congressional_district_geoid (state FIPS x 100 + district number; at-large and DC = SS00). Join key shared with district_layout.json.
fields.district_id: PolicyEngine API public district code (at-large and DC are '-01'), matching the app's DISTRICT_ID.
fields.avg_change: PolicyEngine's average_household_income_change: household-weighted mean of (reform - baseline) household_net_income, USD per household per year, 2026.
fields.share_gaining: Household-weighted share of households whose household_net_income rises by more than 0.1% of baseline (PolicyEngine's winner threshold: (reform-baseline)/max(baseline,1) > 0.001). PolicyEngine itself reports this share person-weighted (pe_winner_percentage_people); this household-weighted version was computed here from the same simulation output.
fields.households: Sum of household_weight in the district (weighted household count, 2026). Equals PolicyEngine's 'population' field, which is a household-weight sum.
fields.sample_households: Unweighted number of microdata household records assigned to the district.
fields.share_gaining_any_increase: Household-weighted share with any positive change in household_net_income (> $0).
fields.share_gaining_over_1usd: Household-weighted share whose household_net_income rises by more than $1 (the definition used in data/national.json winners.share_households_gaining_over_1usd).
fields.share_losing: Household-weighted share losing more than 0.1% of baseline household_net_income.
fields.total_change: Weighted sum of the household_net_income change in the district, USD, 2026.
fields.avg_change_check: Independent recomputation of avg_change from the same output tables; max abs difference is in checks.
fields.pe_*: Fields copied verbatim from PolicyEngine's district_results.

national.total_ctc_change_tax_units_note: Change in the weighted sum of the policyengine-us tax-unit variable 'ctc', whose formula (policyengine_us/variables/gov/irs/credits/ctc/ctc.py) is max(0, ctc_maximum_with_arpa_addition - ctc_phase_out) and does not reference tax liability. It is a diagnostic, not the reform's cost; the change in household net income is total_household_net_income_change.

caveats: District estimates come from filtering one national microdata sample; the number of household records per district ranges from 34 to 1068 (median 114), so individual district values carry sampling noise.

selection.primary: policyengine 6.1.1 bundle (latest policyengine.py release, 2026-09-22; policyengine-us 2.2.1; populace_us_2024 @ populace-us-2024-spm-20260915). Chosen so district figures are consistent with the other data files in this project, which use the same versions.
selection.live_app: On 2026-09-24 https://api.policyengine.org/us/metadata reported policyengine-us 1.764.6 and default dataset hf://policyengine/populace-us/populace_us_2024.h5@populace-us-2024-buildp-sparse-rmloss100-cae8640-20260728T011454Z, and policyengine-api-v2 origin/main (aeae617) pins policyengine==5.2.0 in the simulation executor. That configuration was also run; see live_app_comparison.
selection.dataset_equivalence: populace_us_2024.h5 at populace-us-2024-spm-20260915 (sha256 6496cc43...) and at populace-us-2024-buildp-sparse-rmloss100-cae8640-20260728T011454Z (sha256 48b9d479...) have identical household, tax_unit, spm_unit, family and marital_unit tables and identical person columns; the only difference is one extra person column, is_spm_independent_minor_role, in the spm-20260915 build. household_weight and congressional_district_geoid are identical, so the primary run uses the same weights and district assignment as the live app.
selection.difference_source: Differences between primary and live-app numbers come from the policyengine-us model version (2.2.1 vs 1.764.6) and the policyengine.py version (6.1.1 vs 5.2.0), not from weights.

meta.share_definitions_note: Three household-weighted gainer shares are provided. share_gaining uses PolicyEngine's own winner threshold (gain > 0.1% of baseline household_net_income, from congressional_district_impact.py). share_gaining_over_1usd uses gain > $1, the definition in data/national.json (winners.share_households_gaining_over_1usd). share_gaining_any_increase uses gain > $0. National values: 0.19077518103183919 (PE threshold), 0.19226182079131385 (> $1), 0.19266702520176082 (> $0). Use one definition consistently on screen.

sample_quality.source: household_weight in /Users/maxghenis/PolicyEngine/policyengine-30s/data/compute/districts/pe_data/pe611/populace_us_2024_year_2026.h5 (sha256 22857fed2fa5c2925f3fa17bb7ec0158b7c39884fccc3d7121e8d7453f757314), the exact 2026 weights used
sample_quality.effective_sample_size_definition: Kish: (sum w)^2 / sum(w^2) over the district's household records
sample_quality.interpretation: Each district value is a weighted mean over that district's records in one national sample. With effective sample sizes this small, district values are noisy and should not be presented as precise district facts. A near-zero district means no heavily weighted record in that district gains; it is not a measurement that no families there would gain.
sample_quality.better_source_not_run: policyengine.py docs (docs/microsim.md, origin/main 4dc5959) say congressional-district breakdowns should filter populace_us_2024_acs_local (release manifest: 1,588,854 households, 3,589,209 person rows; calibrated to state and congressional-district population) rather than the national default. It was not run here: the national file (166,321 person rows) took 319 s (baseline) and 468 s (reform) with observed peak RSS of about 9 GB per process; scaling linearly by person rows (21.6x) implies several hours of compute.

fields_added_in_finalize.effective_sample_size: Kish effective sample size of the district's household records under the 2026 weights
fields_added_in_finalize.sample_households_weight_below_1: Number of the district's records with household_weight < 1

meta.runtime_note: runtime_seconds is the wall clock of the compute run that produced these numbers (out/districts_pe611.json); finalize_runtime_seconds is this assembly step.
